Iron Maiden

Author

Andy Field 

library(easystats)
library(tidyverse)

# eddiefy_tib <- here::here("data/eddiefy.csv") |> read_csv()

eddie_tib <- discovr::eddiefy

Introduction

Iron Maiden are a British heavy metal band. Their best albums are

  1. Piece of Mind

  2. Powerslave

CautionHypothesis
  • H1: Iron Maiden songs have got longer over time
  • H0: The length of Iron Maiden songs has not changed over time

The model

  • Outcome: Song duration in seconds (song_duration)
  • Predictor: Number of years since the first album (band_age)

Iron Datum

Load and Look

Table 1 shows some data from spotify, which is stored in the discovr package (Field 2026).

describe_distribution(x = eddie_tib,
                      select = "song_ms",
                      by = "year")

# ms is a horrible unit so let's convert to seconds

eddie_tib <- eddie_tib |> 
  mutate(song_duration = song_ms/1000,
         band_age = year - 1980)
describe_distribution(x = eddie_tib,
                      select = "song_duration",
                      by = "year") |> 
  data_remove(c("Variable", "n_Missing")) |> 
  display()

Visualise

Figure 1 shows a plot of the distributions of song duration and years since the first album as well as a scatterplot.

eddie_tib |> 
  select(band_age, song_duration) |> 
  GGally::ggscatmat()

Evaluate

The model we will fit is

\[ \text{duration} = \hat{b}_{0} + \hat{b}_1\text{years} \]

eddie_lm <- lm(song_duration ~ band_age, data = eddie_tib)
check_model(eddie_lm)

Interpret

Table 2 shows the parameter estimates of the model.

model_parameters(eddie_lm) |> 
  display()
